abstract: The AU library will go through a transformation. This is because a lot of the human resources and efforts are being wasted on simple tasks that can be done by the technology. For instance, there is a staff member who sits at the door of the library and keeps a count of the people going in and out of the library. Our project is aimed at developing and implementing a system that can be used to automate this task within the library. Specifically, we will focus on tracking people entering the library. The goal is to create an automated system which can record the number of visitors in the library each day. And provide a website to display this information. Doing this would allow the staff to engage in more meaningful and valuable tasks. The staff could be employed to assist students, manage the library inventory, or be employed elsewhere within the school. The library would be able to operate more efficiently and for longer every day. Also, the data and statistics collected from the system could be used to make more informed decisions about the library.

domain.label: Library services
domain.evidence: The system automates counting of people entering the AU Library in Hua Mak campus and provides visitor analytics for library staff.

technology.label: TensorFlow
technology.evidence: Software specifications list TensorFlow-GPU 1.14 and the pre-trained ssd_mobilenet_v2_coco object detection model used for people detection.

technology.label: Google Cloud
technology.evidence: Counts are periodically uploaded to a Google Cloud storage bucket and the analytics website is hosted on Google Cloud.

technology.label: Bootstrap
technology.evidence: The website was created using Bootstrap and is also hosted on the same Google Cloud server.

technology.label: imutils
technology.evidence: imutils is listed in the required programs and libraries and passes the video frame by frame to the detector.

technology.label: pandas
technology.evidence: pandas is listed in the software specifications required to run the project.

technology.label: NumPy
technology.evidence: numpy is listed in the software specifications required to run the project.

technology.label: SciPy
technology.evidence: scipy is listed in the software specifications required to run the project.

technology.label: NVIDIA CUDA / cuDNN
technology.evidence: NVIDIA GPU drivers, the NVIDIA CUDA Toolkit and the cuDNN SDK are listed as requirements to run the project.

abstract: RFID (Radio-Frequency Identification) is a powerful technology that uses wireless radio frequency for data communication to automatically identify, and track tags attached to objects. It has been widely applied in various industries such as inventory, logistics, access control and so on. This project aims on digital transformation of library circulation services via RFID solution, in which achieves self-service circulation. Users would be able to borrow books, return books by themselves, simply using the smart circulation platform without the help of librarians. It not only saves the work of librarians, but also provides better service experience for library users.

domain.label: Library services
domain.evidence: The project digitalizes AU Library circulation with an RFID self-service station for borrowing and returning books, and was exhibited at the 50th anniversary of Assumption University.

technology.label: RFID
technology.evidence: SparkFun RFID USB Reader with ID-12LA (125 kHz) cards identify users and UHF tags on books enable bulk reading for self-service circulation.

technology.label: Arduino
technology.evidence: An Arduino UNO R3 programmed in Arduino IDE controls the RFID reader module and communicates with the backend through the serial port.

technology.label: Flask
technology.evidence: Flask and flask_socketio libraries are used for connecting the Python backend and the website frontend.

technology.label: Flask-SocketIO
technology.evidence: Flask and flask_socketio libraries are used for python backend and website frontend connecting, dealing with routing and web-socket data transformation.

technology.label: PySerial
technology.evidence: Pyserial library is used by the python backend for getting data from the serial port sent by the RFID reader and sending commands and data to be written.

abstract: This paper is introducing the platform “AU Competitive Intelligence” which provides insights on how Assumption University performs against its competitors using online sources. The platform performs preprocessing on the incoming flow of unstructured documents into the structural dataset. Also, the platform allows concept learning by utilizing machine learning to classify documents into the field of studies. The platform includes a web interface that shows analysis results being visualized. From this platform, we can quantify the competitiveness of Assumption University with other competing universities in Thailand and also the field of studies. In conclusion, AU Competitive Intelligence is a concept competitive platform to provide a quantifiable presence in online academics.

domain.label: Competitive intelligence
domain.evidence: The platform analyzes the online presence of Assumption University against competitor universities in Thailand so top-level management can evaluate performance and do digital marketing.

technology.label: Amazon Web Services
technology.evidence: AWS is used for the DynamoDB database, AWS Lambda to host analytical functionalities and API Gateway to expose the API endpoints.

technology.label: AWS DynamoDB
technology.evidence: The outcome of the big data processing step is stored into DynamoDB, an Amazon Web Services cloud database platform, with about 502,808 documents ingested.

technology.label: Google Cloud Platform
technology.evidence: A virtual machine hosted on the Google Cloud Platform fetches documents from the search engine and runs the pre-processing pipeline.

technology.label: Google Search API
technology.evidence: Search queries go into Google API and return results in JSON format which are then scraped for documents.

technology.label: scikit-learn
technology.evidence: The whole setup for the machine learning pipeline of Gaussian Naive Bayes, Truncated-SVD and OneVsRestClassifiers was done using the open library Scikit-learn.

technology.label: NLTK
technology.evidence: A predefined list of stopwords was taken from NLTK for the English tokens during preprocessing.

technology.label: PyThaiNLP
technology.evidence: Tokens in th-TH are segmented by using the Pythainlp library.

canonical_title: Case Studies of Fault Tolerance in Numerical Analysis
abstract: A Raspberry Pi cluster combines Raspberry Pi devices in a connected network so that many devices can work together in parallel to increase the overall computing power. This project uses selected numerical approaches to process data with a wireless Raspberry Pi cluster, collect statistical results about the processing time and analyse the fault-tolerance of the wireless network configuration to evaluate the reliability of said cluster for distributed computing.

category.label: Distributed computing
category.evidence: A five-node Raspberry Pi 4 cluster running Hadoop and Spark processes data in parallel and its performance and fault tolerance are experimentally evaluated.

technology.label: Raspberry Pi
technology.evidence: Five Raspberry Pi 4 devices form the cluster, tested wirelessly at distances of 5 to 30 meters from the router and in a wired configuration.

technology.label: Apache Spark
technology.evidence: In the project, Apache Spark is used as a supplement of Hadoop to build large, low latency data analysis, and apps are submitted to the Spark cluster.

technology.label: Apache Hadoop
technology.evidence: The Raspberry Pi cluster is based on Hadoop, using HDFS for distributed storage and MapReduce for distributed computing.

technology.label: PySpark
technology.evidence: Appendix A source code for sentiment analysis imports pyspark.sql and pyspark.ml including HashingTF, IDF, Tokenizer and LogisticRegression.

technology.label: Raspbian
technology.evidence: Raspbian, the official operating system of Raspberry Pi, is downloaded and written to the SD card of each node.

technology.label: Java
technology.evidence: The cluster build step downloads JAVA, Hadoop and Spark on each node and configures environment variables.

technology.label: Apache YARN
technology.evidence: The Spark App is submitted to the YARN cluster where the ResourceManager and NodeManager run the ApplicationMaster and executors.

technology.label: NLTK
technology.evidence: Appendix B word count source code imports nltk and uses nltk.corpus stopwords for tokenization.

technology.label: pyhdfs
technology.evidence: Appendix B source code imports pyhdfs to access HDFS files in the word count program.

canonical_title: August Witcher of the Grand House
abstract: Nowadays, many people like playing games and E-sports has been popular, side-scrolling game is defined as a game that game playing action is viewed from a side-view camera angle, and the onscreen characters can only move to the left or rights to reach the end of the game. Moreover, many people are interested in ghost stories and Thailand is well known for scary stories and some mysterious places so we decided to combine both game and Thai ghost story to make an interesting single game. August Witcher of the Grand House is a side-scrolling game which is designed to attract people who loves playing game with ghost story. In this game, a player will be playing from outside to inside a mysterious house to get through there with some weapons from stage and fight with Thai ghosts. The game is mainly playable on PCs. Our goal is to successfully design and implement our own design of the game on PCs based, and each character's stories Thai ghost concerned to the game more interesting and enjoyable.

technology.label: Adobe Photoshop
technology.evidence: All the design parts of the project such as characters, items and environments were drawn using Photoshop.

technology.label: Unreal Engine Blueprints
technology.evidence: The team learned blueprint technology to build the game, and figures show blueprint modules for jump, movement, animation update and camera placement.
